name: Gateway route registration and boot migrations (P16 EP-387)
skipReason: Boot wiring, not a runtime surface — there is no route that reports it. Verified by tests/platform/gatewayWiring.test.ts (36 assertions over app.ts, the gateway package.json, the migration runner and every migration file) plus a live re-run of all eight P16 migrations against a populated Postgres.
description: Registers each new SDK's Fastify routes and its migrations directory in the gateway's single ordered runMigrations([...]) boot call. Proves all four criteria. The reason this needs an executable guard at all is stated in CLAUDE.md: a missing app.register(...) or a missing runMigrations entry COMPILES, deploys and passes a health check, then 404s or runs against an unmigrated schema — there is no type error and no startup warning, so the wiring has to be asserted against the file that performs it. AC3: for each P16 SDK the test checks three things that must all hold — the package is a gateway dependency (or the import cannot resolve), it is imported as `server as <alias>`, and that alias actually appears in an app.register call; it also asserts NO alias is imported and then forgotten, and that none is registered twice (a duplicate registers every route again and double-runs any onRequest hook). AC1: every package shipping migrations appears in the boot list, and runMigrations is called exactly once. AC2: the runner is forward-only — it keys applied state on UNIQUE (sdk, filename), rejects an edited migration with a sha256 mismatch rather than silently diverging environments, and applies each file in its own BEGIN/ROLLBACK transaction so a failure cannot leave half a schema; on top of that every P16 migration is asserted to use IF NOT EXISTS rather than a bare CREATE, and all eight were re-run against a populated database to confirm it. AC4: ordering is asserted where it actually matters — sdk-lineage precedes sdk-parsing because parsing.extracted_field carries an FK to lineage.node, so the reverse order fails on a fresh database. QA edge cases: migration filenames must be uniquely and monotonically numbered per SDK, since the runner sorts by filename and two files sharing a prefix make the apply order ambiguous between machines; IF NOT EXISTS matters most on a restored snapshot, where a file may be replayed against an existing schema.

testCases.name: Every P16 SDK with a server export is imported and registered
No server alias is imported and then forgotten, and none registered twice
Every package shipping migrations is in the single boot list
All eight P16 migrations re-run cleanly against a populated database
Boot order is dependency-safe where FKs cross SDKs

payload.reason: parsing.extracted_field carries an FK to lineage.node

errorCases.name: An edited migration is refused at boot rather than silently diverging
errorCases.message: [migrator] <sdk>/<file> has changed after being applied (sha256 mismatch). Forward-only — write a new migration.
errorCases.when: an already-applied migration file is edited; without the hash check the edit would apply on fresh environments and not on existing ones, leaving two schemas that disagree with no signal

errorCases.name: A registered SDK missing from the gateway dependencies fails to import
errorCases.when: app.ts imports an SDK that is not a workspace:* dependency of the gateway package.json — per CLAUDE.md both the dependency AND the register line are required, and the build does not warn about the missing pair

errorCases.name: A migration failure rolls back rather than leaving half a schema
errorCases.message: ROLLBACK issued for the failing file
errorCases.when: any statement in a migration file errors; each file runs inside its own transaction, so the schema is left exactly as it was before that file started
